restatement: Change the variable-expression parser so that a pipe inside a single- or double-quoted default text after ?? is kept as part of the default and no longer starts a filter. Pipes outside quotes must split filters exactly as before, including after a quoted default, so later filters still apply to the default. The ?? emptiness rule, the jest suite files and everything outside parser.ts stay untouched, and the node:test suite must still pass.
verification_plan: c1: trace `x ?? "a|b"` through the new split and confirm it yields one part, so the core reaches the ?? handling whole and no filter named `b"` is produced.
c2: trace `x ?? "a|b" | head=2` and confirm exactly two parts (core with the full quoted default, then `head=2`), so head=2 applies to `a|b`.
c3: trace `x ?? 'a|b'` for single quotes; trace `x ?? "d" | trim` and `text | trim | head=3` and confirm the parts are identical to a plain split on every pipe.
m1: look for inputs where a pipe outside quotes no longer splits: a lone apostrophe, an unterminated quote, an escaped quote, mixed quote kinds, and a quoted default followed by several filters.
m2: confirm the diff does not touch the ?? emptiness check or the interpreter.
c4: confirm no jest suite file and no frozen test appears in the diff, that any path outside parser.ts has a scope exception row, and check what evidence there is that the suite passes.
Rubric: both quote kinds are honoured; the scan is a bounded single pass with no new throw on escaped or unbalanced quotes; there are no unrelated edits in parser.ts.
f1: re-run the earlier reproductions (`x ?? "a\"b" | trim`, `x ?? "abc | trim`, `x ?? it's | trim`) against the revised split.

findings.title: A quoted default that holds both an escaped quote and a pipe still splits at the pipe (unchanged from base)

serves.scenario: `${{x ?? "a\"|b"}}` with x missing: the backslash-escaped quote closes the quoted run, the pipe splits, and `b"` is treated as a filter name, so the default does not render whole. Base behaved the same way, so this is not a regression or a new error type, and the spec does not define escapes; noted for the lead only.

findings.rubric: A default with an escaped or unbalanced quote does not hang or throw a new error type.
findings.reproduction: Call splitOutsideQuotes on `x ?? "a\"|b"` with separator `|`: it returns 2 parts (`x ?? "a\"` and `b"`), the same as base `expr.split('|')`. Rendering with x missing should give the same Unknown filter error at base and at head.

evidence: test:dp-03 a lone apostrophe in an unquoted default still lets the pipe split off the filter
test:dp-03 an unterminated double quote in a default still lets the pipe split off the filter
